04. 1.

This matter is taken up by through hybrid arrangement (virtual/physical mode).
2.

The Appellant, by filing this application, has prayed for suspension of further execution of sentence imposed upon him in Spl.G.R. No.71 of 2018, by the learned Presiding Officer, Exclusive Special Court Established under SC & ST (POA) Act, Bolangir under section 389 Cr.P.C and his release on bail pending disposal of this Appeal.
3.

Learned counsel for the Appellant submits that this Appellant having been convicted for commission of offence under section 376(2)(j)/376(2)(i) of the IPC read with section 3(2)(v) of the SC & ST (POA) Act has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life with fine and default stipulation for the offences under the IPC and for the offence under the SC & ST (POA) Act he has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period of 10 years with fine with default stipulation for the offences punishable under section 376(2)(j)/376(2)(i) of the IPC.

She submits that the Appellant has been in custody from 07.10.2018 and there is no evidence on record to show that the Appellant committed the said offence knowing the victim to be a member of the Scheduled Tribe.

She further submits that the victim during her cross- examination in the trial with the assistance of the mother- interpreter has stated all in support of the fact as if the sexual relationship was consensual.

She, therefore, submits that there is every chance of success in this Appeal and as the Appeal is not likely to be heard and disposed of so soon, further execution of sentence be suspended and the Appellant be released on bail pending disposal of this Appeal.
4. Learned counsel for the State opposes the move.

According to him, the provision of section 8(C)
of the SC & ST (POA) Act reads that with the proven fact that the victim is a member of Scheduled Dhanapati Meher vs State Of Odisha on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191497828/

entities.text: Scheduled Dhanapati Meher vs State Of Odisha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Caste or Scheduled Tribe as the case may be, a presumption would arise that such was within the knowledge of the offender.

He further submits that such a presumption being irrebuttable, it is open for the offender either to bring out any material to dislodge such presumption or to lead some evidence to show that said fact could not have come to his knowledge at the time of commission of offence or even thereafter in case, it is a continuing offence.

He next inviting the attention of this Court to paragraph-2 of the deposition of the victim-P.W.25, he submits that the same speaks for itself when the demeanor of the victim has been recorded by the Trial Court that the witness being asked by the mother, could not be able to answer, because she all the time concentrated on the Appellant and for that the scene was to be switched off.
He, therefore, submits that it is not a fit case for acceptance of the prayer advanced in the application.

5. Taking into account the submissions made and on going through the judgment passed by the Trial Court, more particularly, the deposition of victim-P.W.25, who happens to be an illiterate deaf and dumb girl

; at this stage, we do not find it to be a fit case for acceptance of the prayers relating to suspension of further execution of sentence and release of the Appellant on bail pending disposal of the Appeal.
6. The I.A is accordingly dismissed.
(D. Dash), Judge.
